summary: Upshur County, TX Texas Forest Service tower listed as gone; 1960 radio relay plan and 1965 fire report name crew leader Carl Stewart; no build date or site description found.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no removal date or site description found

events.note: New radio relay system installed to link the Gilmont tower with the Hallsville and Negley towers and the Linden district headquarters
Two fires spotted August 17 in northeast Upshur County; a later report raised the possibility of malicious mischief
Crew leader Carl Stewart was described as in charge of the Gilmont tower

evidence.supports: Tower location about five miles northeast of Gilmer; 1960 relay installation
evidence.quote: A new radio relay system is being installed at the Texas Forest Service fire lookout tower at Gilmont, five miles northeast of Gilmer.

evidence.supports: Relay links Gilmont with Hallsville, Negley and Linden; ready by January; crew leader Carl Stewart
evidence.quote: Crew Leader Carl Stewart explained that the new relay system, which will be ready by January, will provide more reliable communication between the towers here, at Hallsville and Negley and with the Texas Forest Service District headquarters at Linden.

evidence.supports: Purpose of radio contact: locate fires from smoke, dispatch equipment
evidence.quote: Radio communication is necessary to quickly locate fires from smoke, and to dispatch fire fighting equipment.

evidence.supports: Agency and county heading of the Gilmont page
Two fires spotted August 17 in northeast Upshur County
evidence.quote: Two fires in a northeast section of Upshur County were spotted on August 17

evidence.supports: Crew leader Carl Stewart filed a report raising malicious mischief
evidence.quote: a later investigative report by Texas Forest Service crew leader Carl Stewart indicated there might have been malicious mischief behind their cause.

evidence.supports: Stewart described as in charge of the Gilmont tower
evidence.quote: who is in charge of the Gilmont Fire Lookout Tower.

evidence.supports: Both clippings are from The Gilmer Mirror
Index lists the Gilmont tower as a tower with status Gone, with coordinates

corrections.why: The Forest Lookouts Gilmont page is headed 'Upshur County - Texas Forest Service' and both clippings concern Upshur County; 'Upshire' appears to be a typo, repeated in the FFLA index.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: two sources, both secondary. The Forest Lookouts page reprints two Gilmer Mirror clippings (1960, 1965). No build date, design, height or site description was found. Staffing is inferred from the 1965 'in charge of' wording, not from a staffing record. The 1960 clipping's cost figure (about $200,000) is not used because it is unclear what it covers. The FFLA index also spells the county 'Upshire', so the county correction also applies to that page's row. Two WebSearch calls turned up no other page on this tower. No photo found.
